transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-24
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Maria Chen (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (CTO - Nimbus), Liam O'Neill (Head of Infra - Nimbus), Rachel Gomez (PM - Nimbus)

Summary: Quick sync to align on rollout plan for the POC -> production cutover, canary and A/B strategies, monitoring and runbooks. Action items and owners captured at the end.

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining on the 24th, i know folks are heads down for year end so appreciate the time. quick roll call?
[00:05] Aisha: Aisha here.
[00:06] Liam: Liam.
[00:07] Rachel: Rachel.
[00:08] Samir: and Maria from my side. ok great, agenda: cutover approach, canary vs a/b, monitoring & alerts, runbooks/rollback, dependencies (kms/soc2/legal), and confirm next steps.

[00:28] Maria: quick status - the model tuning we ran last week improved hallucination rate on the 2k prompt set by about 18%, latency at 95th is around 310ms on the dedicated pool with the current batch settings; we still see a tail when concurrency spikes.

[00:42] Liam: that tail's our main worry. if spikes map to patient-facing flows we need a fallback plan. what's the tradeoff if we increase batching? i.e. smaller cost but higher p95.

[00:50] Maria: right, smaller batch sizes reduces p95 but increases per-token cost. For go-live we suggested a hybrid policy: keep small batches for low concurrency routes (critical endpoints) and enable batching for background / async workflows. Redwood Console gives token-level breakdown so you can see cost impact per route.

[01:12] Rachel: can we do a canary that routes 5% of traffic to Redwood Dedicated and keep the rest on Hosted? or do we need a mirrored VPC canary?

[01:20] Samir: both are possible. two common patterns: 1) traffic-splitting canary where 5-10% of real traffic hits the new infra (we do gradual ramp) or 2) mirrored canary where staging traffic is replayed into the new stack. Mirror avoids user exposure but misses real-time edge cases. For patient-facing stuff we usually recommend mirrored + a small live canary after smoke tests.

[01:48] Aisha: legal will want mirrored first - they don't want any patient-facing drift during rollouts. so mirrored for the first week, then live 1% canary.

[01:56] Maria: technical note: for a mirrored canary we'll need KV cache sync or a warmed state otherwise latency and failure modes differ. sometimes the 'KV cache' gets cold, which makes the canary look worse than production. we'll include cache warm-up in the runbook.

[02:14] Liam: about KMS: we have a customer-managed key for PHI. do we need to change anything for Dedicated?

[02:20] Samir: Redwood Private / Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS via our KMS integration - you'll provide the key ARN and we integrate with the control plane. For hosted we can also support a split-key approach but for compliance we recommend Dedicated with your CMK.

[02:36] Aisha: ok that's good. SOC2 docs - we reviewed what you sent, but security needs a little more detail on audit logs and key rotation policy during cutover.

[02:46] Samir: i'll push an updated section on audit logs and rotation into the runbook; Maria will attach the Console screenshots for retention windows and where to find per-token traces.

[02:58] Rachel: on rollback criteria - what metrics constitute an automatic rollback vs manual intervention?

[03:05] Maria: recommended thresholds: if error-rate (5xx) increases > 1% absolute over baseline AND latency p95 increases > 40% for 5 minutes, auto-switch to fallback model/region. for critical endpoints we prefer manual rollback with alerts to on-call + runbook steps. we can wire these into your pager/splunk/new relic - Redwood has webhook and tracing integrations.

[03:32] Liam: do we have test harness that can run the smoke tests during the canary? we'd like to run synthetic traffic every 2 minutes.

[03:38] Samir: yes, we can provide a small runner and a sample test suite; Maria will share the smoke test templates. recommended check: correctness on 100 canonical prompts, token output length distributions, response time, and a small set of negative tests for hallucinations.

[03:55] Aisha: what about A/B experiments? we'd like to compare two model variants for quality AND cost. is that supported in the rollout?

[04:01] Maria: Redwood supports route-based A/B. you can shard traffic with weight and collect per-route metrics; Console gives side-by-side per-model latency/cost/quality metrics. for the POC we can do a short 48-hour A/B on non-critical flows.

[04:18] Rachel: timeline: our target tentative go-live is Jan 6th. is that realistic?

[04:22] Samir: tight but doable. critical path: staging mirror up, KMS integration, runbook & smoke tests, legal signoff, and final canary ramp. i'd push to Jan 8th to be safe but if Nimbus confirms stakeholders we can aim Jan 6th.

[04:40] Liam: provisioning the staging VPC mirror is our blocker - i'll aim to have that by Dec 28th.

[04:44] Aisha: legal turnaround is slow during holidays, i may not get signoff until Dec 30th.

[04:49] Maria: note on metrics and monitoring - we'll set up dashboards: latency p50/p95/p99, token breakdown, error rates, user-visible errors, and model-quality drift (we can plug in a sampling-based eval to flag regressions). Alerts: page on high error-rate, slack alert for quality regressions.

[05:08] Rachel: what about runbooks - can you draft a cutover checklist vs rollback checklist? we need clear owner at each step.

[05:13] Samir: yes - high level cutover steps: 1) freeze config, 2) warm KV cache, 3) run smoke tests on mirrored traffic, 4) small live canary (1-5%), 5) monitor 30-60 mins, 6) ramp to 25/50/100 per plan. rollback: 1) auto-detect triggers, 2) switch routing to fallback model or region, 3) notify on-call, 4) run postmortem. i'll draft this and map owners.

[05:38] Maria: checklist will also include traffic-shift API calls, health-check endpoints, and where to find fallback toggles in Console. note - toggles require AE or customer admin perms.

[05:47] Liam: permissions - we'll need RBAC entries for service accounts that run the canary. also want audit trail.

[05:52] Samir: agreed - we'll include RBAC steps and audit log locations.

[05:55] Aisha: data residency question - the mirrored traffic will contain PHI, so it must stay in our EU region. can Redwood guarantee region isolation for the mirror?

[06:02] Maria: yes, we can route mirrored traffic to a Dedicated pool in your EU region; we'll also configure retention to meet your policy.

[06:09] Rachel: do we need to change model size/quantization for go-live to reduce cost? we were on a 8-bit quantized variant during POC.

[06:16] Maria: 8-bit quant works well; if you need lower cost we can suggest a quant profile and smaller model variant. tradeoff: slight quality regression but large cost wins. we'll include recommended profiles in the runbook.

[06:30] Samir: ok let's confirm concrete next steps and owners - (verbal recap) Samir will draft runbook, Maria will provide canary config and smoke tests, Liam will provision staging VPC, Rachel will finalize acceptance criteria, Aisha will coordinate legal.

[06:50] Rachel: one more ask - can you share a sample incident playbook template we can adapt for internal on-call?

[06:54] Maria: yes, we have a playbook template; i'll attach and mark required fields.

[06:58] Samir: great. any final Qs?

[07:02] Aisha: none from legal now.

[07:04] Liam: no.

[07:05] Rachel: all good. thanks.

[07:07] Samir: thanks everyone, i'll shoot the runbook by Monday (Dec 27) and Maria will follow with configs. we'll reconvene next week same time unless we need an ad-hoc during cutover.

Recap / Next steps: see action_items above.

References mentioned: Redwood Console screenshots (link sent in thread), Runbook template (Samir to share), Smoke test templates (Maria), SOC2 + audit logs doc (security pack link).

End of transcript.
